one_liner: Single-header C (C++-compatible) RNG library whose ziggurat standard-normal sampler measured 2.2x (float) and 4.2x (double) faster than std::normal_distribution.
what_it_does: cauldron/random.h is a literate, stb-style single-file C library (define RANDOM_H_IMPLEMENTATION in exactly one translation unit) with OS TRNG wrappers, PRNGs (PCG, Romu, xoshiro/xoroshiro, middle-square Weyl, ChaCha), uniform integer/real distributions, normal distributions and shuffling. For normals you fill a table once with dist_normalf_zig_init / dist_normal_zig_init and then call dist_normalf_zig(&table, rand32, &rng) or dist_normal_zig(&table, rand64, &rng), passing your own generator as a function pointer plus state; it returns a standard normal, so the caller scales and shifts. It also offers a table-free ratio-of-uniforms dist_normal(f) and an approximate popcount-based dist_normalf_fast.
how_it_is_fast: It is the Marsaglia-Tsang ziggurat in Doornik's formulation, but with a single table of box x-coordinates (129 floats for the default 128 boxes, 257 doubles for the default 256); the source comment says dropping the second bound table halves memory and allows bigger tables. Each sample usually costs one RNG call, one multiply and one compare, because one 32- or 64-bit draw is split into the sign (bit 0), the box index (the next 7 or 8 bits) and the uniform (the top 24 or 53 bits). Only rejected draws reach the wedge test (two expf/exp calls) or Marsaglia's 1964 log-based tail method.
when_to_use: C or C++ simulation and Monte Carlo code that draws many scalar standard normals and where std::normal_distribution shows up in profiles (about 9-17 ns per sample in the cited run versus about 4 ns).
Projects that want a vendorable MIT single header with no dependency beyond libm that builds as C89 and as C++ (both are exercised by the repo's test script).
Code that already controls its own fast PRNG (Romu, PCG, xoshiro**) and wants to plug it in per thread through the function-pointer interface.
Float sampling where a small (516-byte, 129 floats) read-only table that stays in L1 is acceptable.
when_not_to_use: Bulk or SIMD fills of large arrays: the routine is scalar, one sample per call; vectorized siblings such as EigenRand target that case.
Code that needs the <random> distribution-object interface (URBG, param_type, mean/stddev) or other distributions such as gamma or Student t.
Results that must be bit-identical to std::normal_distribution or another library: the sequence differs.

Pairing it with a generator whose low bits are weak (the + and * scramblers, plain power-of-two LCGs): the sign and box index come from the lowest bits of each draw, while random.h's own notes say the xoshiro/xoroshiro + variants' lower bits fail linear tests yet recommend those variants for floating point.
Decisions that need hard numbers: the only published comparison is a first-party 2020 run of precursor code with no CPU, compiler or flags; re-measure on your target.

integration.dependencies: libm (logf/expf/sqrtf and the double versions); the TRNG section uses OS APIs (getrandom, arc4random, RtlGenRandom or /dev/urandom), not needed by the ziggurat
integration.min_toolchain: C89 (test script builds with -std=c89 -Dinline=) or C++ via g++ -xc++; requires uint32_t/uint64_t and float/double formats with at least 7 spare bits beyond the mantissa (checked by #error)
integration.platforms: any (portable C, no intrinsics in the ziggurat path); the test script also runs a big-endian MIPS build under qemu when that toolchain is installed
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the table is read-only after init and taken as a const pointer, and RNG state is caller-owned, so one shared table plus one RNG state per thread works by construction

gotchas: You must call dist_normalf_zig_init / dist_normal_zig_init before sampling. Table size is a compile-time macro: DIST_NORMALF_ZIG_COUNT defaults to 128 and cannot exceed 128; DIST_NORMAL_ZIG_COUNT defaults to 256 (power of two, at most 1024). The matching _R and _AREA constants are only defined when you leave COUNT at its default, so a custom COUNT needs its own constants from tools/random/ziggurat-constants.c.

Because the sign and box index use the low bits of each draw, a generator with poor low bits biases the output; a related issue (#2, closed 2024-11-22) showed dist_uniform*_dense returning only 1.0 with the odd-only randu LCG.

The repo's CI runs test/random/dist_normal.c (Jochen Voss's GPL-2 testgauss checks of mean and tail probabilities, with Romu generators) under gcc, sanitizers and g++, but test.sh ends with 'exit 0' and has no 'set -e', so a failing test would not fail CI. The GPL applies to that test file only; random.h itself is MIT.
dist_normalf_fast is an approximation (sum of popcounts plus a linear nudge), not an exact normal sampler; do not confuse it with the ziggurat functions.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick cauldron when you want plain C (even C89) and a scalar standard-normal function driven by your own PRNG; its precursor ran about 1.8x faster than the existing ziggurat in miloyip's normaldist-benchmark. Pick EigenRand for vectorized bulk fills on Eigen arrays, Zest for a C++ distribution-object API covering gamma, Student t and other ziggurat-able distributions, and cxx-ziggurat or zigg if you prefer a C++ class or R integration.
verified_claims_summary: In camel-cdr's issue #3 on miloyip/normaldist-benchmark (2020-12-19; 1M samples, minimum of 10 trials; CPU and compiler not stated), a template ziggurat that is the precursor of random.h's code took 4.018 ns per float and 4.081 ns per double, against 8.852 and 17.009 ns for std::normal_distribution driven by std::minstd_rand and 7.289 and 7.817 ns for the benchmark's existing ziggurat. That code fed the ziggurat from the Numerical Recipes 32-bit LCG, taking the box index from its low 7 bits, and built the double version's 64-bit draw from two identically seeded copies of that LCG, so both halves are equal; no output-quality result was reported, and the repo's own tools/random/bench.c times dist_normal(f)_zig but publishes no numbers.
status_note: Stale (random.h last changed 2025-02-01, 'small changes'; 0 open issues, 143 stars) but MIT-licensed, self-contained and easy to vendor; the ziggurat section can be copied on its own per the header's design notes.
